title: Entropy Methods in Combinatorics Lab
summary: Entropy as a counting technology: choose an object of a finite family uniformly, so H(X) = log |F|, encode it by coordinates, bound the information with an entropy inequality and exponentiate. Thirty-four lessons from uniform entropy, the chain rule, conditioning and subadditivity through the binomial and multinomial bounds, mutual information and KL divergence, Shearer, combinatorial Shearer and Loomis–Whitney, fractional covers and hypergraphs, to perfect matchings and Bregman's theorem by random reveal order, with compression, typical sets, the method of types, set systems, antichains and a sumset glimpse. Explore, Guided, Problems (a sixteen-step ladder with progressive hints), Compare and Encode modes; a Shearer cover builder, projection and matching labs; an entropy ledger with slack, proof architecture, bits or nats, a command palette and deep links. Every number is an exact count against the entropy bound, checked by built-in self-tests. Present any proof or export it as a narrated beamdswitch deck. Works offline, from file:// and in an iframe.
